headline.text: Commercial elevators and port terminals held 7.25 million tonnes of grain in the week ending 4 October 2026. Higher than in any of the previous 5 years for this time of year (2% above the median). Worth a closer look; not by itself a sign of crisis.
3.21 million tonnes of grain were exported from port terminals in the 4 weeks to 4 October 2026. Within the range of the previous 5 years for this time of year (4% above the median).

Of 12 tracked wholesale prices in Toronto, 2 are higher and 2 lower than in any recent year at this time of year, after adjusting for inflation; 4 are within the usual range, and 4 lack enough history to compare.
In October 2026, prices of food bought in stores were +2.0% on a year earlier; average hourly wages were +2.2%. Wages have risen faster than store food prices for 2 months in a row.
GDACS lists 8 orange or red hazard alerts worldwide. 4 are in countries Canada has recently imported tracked foods or farm inputs from; that is a supplier link, not evidence of an effect on Canada.
